title: One dropped frame permanently shifts every later row's capture instant by one shot period, still labelled capture_source=gpio_edge
goal_clause: "each image being taken <10ms from eachother" + "matched to metadata available at time image was taken"
failure: Substantially as claimed, with one branch the claim omits. Any frame that fires but never lands as a valid file - a camera-side drop, or the certain code paths in _handle where a pull fails (download error, size mismatch, bad SOI/EOI) or the local write raises OSError, all of which mark the frame `seen` in _poll_once first and return without popping _cmds - leaves its command in the queue. (a) If that fire produced an EXPOSURE edge (always true for the pull-failure paths, since the shutter did fire), the next frame takes the stale command and its matching edge: every subsequent row on that camera is stamped exactly one shot period early, still labelled capture_source=gpio_edge with time_err_ms=0.0, with nav_snapshot()/imu_snapshot() queried at the wrong instant and _fmt_fname writing the same wrong epoch into the filename, so filename-based stereo pairing pairs cam2 frame N with cam1 frame N-1. (b) If the fire produced no edge at all, the head command matches nothing inside the 0.20 s window, so every following frame silently degrades to capture_source=exif for ~5 s and then, when the line-240 age-out finally pops, jumps forward by many periods at once. Both branches persist for the rest of the run unless capture pauses long enough (or pull lag grows enough) to push the head command past the 5 s age-out, and neither is visible in flight_log.csv, run.json, PullWorker.stats() jitter, or Anomalies.scan().
fix: Do not let a frame inherit an unclaimed command. Have piagent return a monotonic sequence number with each exposure edge and have /gpio/fire echo the sequence it produced, so frame->fire pairing is by identity, not by position in a queue. Failing that, make _capture_instant reject a match whose command is older than the previous frame's command by more than one nominal period, drop the orphan command, and emit a warn event with a per-run counter of orphaned fires so the operator sees the run went off-by-one.

title: A node that fires late or does not fire at all is never detected: late_ms/ok/actual_epoch are discarded, capture_once always returns ok:True, and in auto-capture its return value is thrown away
goal_clause: "each image being taken <10ms from eachother" and "Good logic to defensively handle and altert for missing sensors or cameras or missing data"
failure: Accurate failure mode: the Jetson never records or alerts on per-shot fire outcome, so a run can silently miss the rig's primary <10 ms spec and no operator-facing signal exists. A late fire is NOT recorded as falsified data: match_exposure_edge matches on expected=target within the 200 ms window and returns the kernel epoch_hw of the real edge, so the flight_log datetime is the TRUE exposure instant and nav (fix_at) / IMU (+/-100 ms) are sampled at it; the pair is desynchronised but each row is individually truthful, and the skew is recoverable post-hoc by differencing the two cameras' flight_logs. Beyond 200 ms no edge matches and the row falls back to capture_source="exif" (whole-second EXIF + calibrated offset), which is self-labelling rather than a false gpio_edge claim. Reachable ok:false paths are "trigger line unavailable" (driver.shot returns None), the subprocess-pulse failure on the fallback path, "no gpio on this node" on stale health, and http_json's {"ok": false, "_unreachable": true} on timeout -- NOT the 409, which capture_once cannot provoke. When a node genuinely takes no picture, the claim's "not one event is emitted, empty events.log" is wrong: events.log still carries an info "manual capture fired" per shot naming that node with path "gpio"; the UI fleet card shows live per-node "pulled ok / N fail / jit" (rig_ui.html:308); an HTTP-timeout fire stalls the capture thread until the auto loop emits warn "capture backlog: N shots still in flight" (run.py:632-638); and a dead piagent is separately caught as node_offline/camera_absent. The real defect is therefore the absence of any capture_fail / gpio_late alert and of any per-shot sync-quality record on the Jetson, plus rig_ui.html:572-573 listing a node that returned ok:false as "captured", leaving the operator to notice a non-firing camera only by watching a passive counter.
fix: In capture_once, after joining the fire threads, compute each node's realised exposure instant (`actual_epoch + trig_latency[node]`) and the pairwise spread; emit a warn/error event and an `sync_skew` / `capture_miss` anomaly whenever any node reports ok:false, |late_ms| exceeds a budget (~2 ms, not 50 ms), or the spread exceeds 10 ms; append the per-shot skew to run.json and show it in the UI; return ok:False when any node failed to fire.

title: Starting a run with auto_capture races trigger calibration against survey capture, then marks the real survey frames as already-seen so they are never pulled, renamed, or logged
goal_clause: "Images from each cameras renamed from camera and matched to metadata available at time image was taken, saved as csv flight_log" and "Keep things organized by transect"
failure: Starting a run with the UI defaults (auto_capture checked, calibrate defaulted to True) runs ~14 s of trigger calibration concurrently with the auto-capture loop, and _calibrate_then_reset (run.py:857-860) then marks every file currently on each node as already-seen. The magnitude in the original claim is overstated: _poll_once adds a name to `seen` before downloading (run.py:166-168), so already-listed, in-flight and failed frames are already seen; the frames actually destroyed are only those that appeared on the node since that worker's last listing — typically 1-3 per camera at 2 fps, unbounded only when the pull worker lags. Those frames are never pulled, renamed or written to flight_log.csv, the count differs per camera so stereo pairs break asymmetrically, and nothing reports it (run.json's `frames` is just the pulled count, with no comparison against node frame count). The metadata damage is worse than claimed in the other direction: the ~6 calibration frames per camera that the worker does pull before the reset are not merely logged as survey frames — in _capture_instant (run.py:229-247) each one claims the oldest queued auto-capture command and the edge nearest it, consuming a real survey frame's command/edge pairing; and after reset_edge_cursors() empties _edge_buf (863, 867-876), the stale _cmds entries for the discarded frames are only dropped once older than 5 s (240-246), so subsequent frames fail the 0.20 s match window in match_exposure_edge (739-794) and fall back to capture_source=exif for several seconds.
fix: Do not start the capture loop until calibration has completed — either await `_calibrate_then_reset` when `auto_capture` is set, or skip run-start calibration and use the startup figure. Baseline only the frame names calibration itself produced (diff the shots list before/after each calibration fire) instead of everything on the camera, and tag calibration frames so the pull worker discards them by name rather than by a blanket seen-refresh.

title: IMU sample epochs are stamped at parse time, not sample time, so the "nearest" sample is nearest by arrival, not by exposure
goal_clause: "Collect external metadata from ... IMU sources" bound to the capture instant
failure: imu_yb._Decoder.sample() stamps s["epoch"] = time.time() when the parser reaches the frame (L116), and _loop calls _publish() once per chunk that yielded no orientation frame (L222-225). Because want = self._ser.in_waiting or 1 (L203) returns a chunk as soon as any byte arrives, most chunks contain no complete frame at all, so _publish() appends an exact duplicate of the previous sample - orientation, inertial, and baro alike - under a fresh epoch. Measured live on cam1: the device's orientation actually updates every 40 ms (25 Hz), not every 5 ms; the ring's apparent ~190 Hz is manufactured by duplicates, and only 16% of ring entries (10 of 63 over a 326 ms window) have an epoch that corresponds to a real orientation update; 53 of 62 consecutive entries carry identical roll/pitch/yaw. run.py's imu_snapshot() min(|s.epoch - capture|) therefore almost always selects a duplicate and reports _age_s of p50 6.7 ms / max 17 ms while the attitude it writes is actually p50 19.5 ms / p95 38 ms / max 40 ms old - an understatement of up to 40 ms, four times the rig's whole sync budget. The error is invisible: _age_s is never written to FLIGHT_HEADER, and the 100 ms IMU_MAX_AGE_S gate is justified by run.py:671's false "<5 ms at 200 Hz" invariant, so imu_stall never fires. The same duplicate stream keeps latest()["epoch"] perpetually fresh, so a partial IMU failure (fusion output frozen while bytes keep flowing) is undetectable by piagent._acquire_loop's staleness check or by run.py's stall warning. Intra-chunk batching (~2 ms) and USB/scheduler late bias (~1-3 ms) are real but secondary to the duplicate-publish mechanism.
fix: Derive the sample epoch from the chunk read instant minus a measured per-frame offset, or at minimum stamp once per read() and interpolate frames within the chunk at the nominal 5 ms cadence. Only append to the ring when an orientation frame actually updated the values, and mark ring entries with which sub-frames are fresh.

title: Default desired vector sets TransSize=Small, so every archived transect image is a downscaled review JPEG
goal_clause: "Images from each cameras renamed from camera and matched to metadata available at time image was taken, saved as csv flight_log ... Keep things organized by transect"
failure: DEFAULT_DESIRED (rigcore.py:362) and the live saved vector /home/wildtech/rig/desired.json both set transsize:1 (Small), which the convergence layer pushes to every body. Verified live: the host copies served by ilxctl /shot/<name> - the exact bytes run.py's PullWorker archives into <run>/camN/ and rows into flight_log.csv - are 1616x1080 JPEGs (~200-330 KB) on both cam1 and cam2, i.e. 1.7 MP instead of the sensor's 61 MP. So every image the run pipeline produces is a review-grade thumbnail unsuitable for photogrammetry, and the only survey-grade frames are the full-res JPEGs left on each camera's SD card, for which the codebase offers no download path (no card/contents endpoint exists in src/main.cpp or piagent.py). Recovery is possible but manual: physically offload both cards and join ILX*.JPG names to flight_log rows using the "orig" field in run.json's index or the "<renamed> <- <orig>" lines in the run's events.log. flight_log.csv itself lacks an original-filename column (run.py:28-33), which does contradict docs/PROTOCOL.md:169's claim that the original name is retained "in flight_log and run.json". transsize can be corrected today via POST /api/settings {"transsize":0} even though rig_ui.html neither shows nor sets it.
fix: Default transsize to 0 (Original) for survey work, or make it an explicit UI choice: add filetype / imagesize / transsize / store_dest / drive selects to the Controls exposure card built from the body's choice lists (camera.cpp:1625-1640 already emits them), surface the current values in `_node_view`, and add the original camera filename as a flight_log.csv column so card originals remain joinable.

title: Controls tab never reads back the desired vector; Apply re-pushes hardcoded f/8 1/200 ISO400 over the fleet's real settings
goal_clause: "Settings are adjusted then applied to all cameras" / "UI is intuitive, easy to use"
failure: The exposure inputs (rig_ui.html:216-218) are never hydrated from the server, so on every fresh page load they show f/8, 1/200, ISO 400 regardless of the fleet's real state, and btnApply (rig_ui.html:560-564) posts all three, driving SettingsManager.update() -> reconcile_all(force=True) into both bodies. Two corrections to the reported failure. (1) The claim that the tab "never reads back" is too strong: renderCtlLive() at rig_ui.html:612 does paint each connected camera's real aperture/shutter/ISO into the #clx-<node> span in the live-view header, refreshed every second from /api/fleet -- so the operator sees a mismatched form next to a correct readout, and the header reflects the clobber ~1s later. The defect is that the input fields, and only they, are stale. (2) The hypothetical f/5.6 1/500 ISO 800 case understates the live one: ~/rig/desired.json on this Jetson currently holds aperture=800, shutter=65736 (both matching the HTML literals) and iso=16777215, which is ISO_AUTO (rigcore.py:78, docs/PROTOCOL.md:58). So today, any Apply silently converts the fleet from auto-ISO to a fixed ISO 400 mid-survey -- exactly the regression rigcore.py's own _load() docstring warns about for the missing-file path -- and because #sIso is a bare type="number" input with no AUTO affordance, auto-ISO cannot be restored from the UI at all afterwards. The aperture/shutter clobber is latent, only reachable once someone changes them away from f/8 1/200. The EV half of the claim is real but display-only and non-destructive: Apply never posts expcomp, and bumpEv (line 559) assigns from the server's authoritative r.expcomp_mev, so the stale "0 mEV" misleads only until the first bump.
fix: On tab activation, GET /api/settings and populate sAp/sSh/sIso/sExpMode/evVal from the live desired vector (and re-sync after every successful Apply); send only fields the user actually edited (dirty-tracking) so an untouched control can never overwrite desired.

title: focus_position and zoom_position are never part of desired, so a rebooted camera silently comes back at a different focus than its stereo partner
goal_clause: "Settings are adjusted then applied to all cameras" (identically configured stereo pair for photogrammetry)
failure: Lens position is pure fire-and-forget: rigd.py:522-526 hands /api/focus/position, /api/zoom/position and /api/zoom/setting to Rig.fanout, which writes only to monitors currently in CAM_CONNECTED and persists nothing, and no focus/zoom position field exists in CONVERGE_FIELDS or DEFAULT_DESIRED so nothing ever re-asserts it. The trigger is broader and cheaper than a full reboot: any node not in CAM_CONNECTED at the moment the operator moves the slider — including the ordinary re-claim window, where NodeMonitor backs off 5-60 s and _startup_calibrate allows up to 90 s — is silently skipped, and the POST still returns {"ok": true} with that node merely absent from `results`, so neither the UI nor the event log records that only one camera was configured. After any dropout, reconnect or body power-cycle, the lens comes back at whatever position the body/lens restored (not necessarily its pre-fault value), and rigd never re-drives it. Meanwhile _reconcile_node restores aperture, shutter, ISO, drive, store_dest and focus MODE and publishes convergence.synced=true, because the synced badge is computed only over CONVERGE_FIELDS. The operator has no way to see the divergence: Rig._node_view exposes no focusPos/zoomPos, and the Controls-tab slider is write-only and never reflects any camera's actual position. Every subsequent stereo pair is shot at mismatched focus/zoom — differing interior orientation, which invalidates the photogrammetry solution — while the UI asserts the fleet is in lock-step.
fix: Record focus_position / zoom_setting / zoom_position into `desired` whenever the fanout lens endpoints succeed, add them to CONVERGE_FIELDS against the readback keys ilxctl already emits (`focusPosCur`, `zoomSetting`, `zoomPosCur`, camera.cpp:1600-1614), and re-push them on reconnect like every other field.

title: The exposure panel never reads back the fleet's actual settings, so pressing Apply reverts every camera to the page's hard-coded defaults
goal_clause: "Settings are adjusted then applied to all cameras"
failure:
The mechanism is exactly as claimed, but three details in the stated failure are imprecise:

(a) The `auto:{on:false}` half is inert, not harmful. `POST /api/settings/auto` -> `SettingsManager.set_auto()` (`rigcore.py:422-426`) only sets `self._auto`, which is never read anywhere in rigcore.py, rigd.py or run.py — the only other references are its `__init__` and its echo in `get()`. The "Auto (ISO servo)" mode is unimplemented dead state, so resetting `#sExpMode` to manual changes nothing on the cameras. The damage is entirely from the three exposure numbers.

(b) "The operator's mental model of the fleet's exposure is wrong on every page load" is overstated for aperture/shutter/ISO: the same Controls tab renders the true per-camera exposure in `renderCtlLive` (`rig_ui.html:611`, `#clx-<node>` = `n.aperture n.shutter n.iso`), and the Fleet cards show an "Exposure" row from the same readback. The real values are on screen — just not in the boxes Apply will post. The EV part of the claim does hold fully: `expcomp` has no readback key in `CONVERGE_FIELDS` (`rigcore.py:342-351`), and `#evVal` is written only inside `bumpEv`, so `desired['expcomp']` is genuinely invisible in the UI after any reload.

(c) Apply does not clobber EV. `btnApply` posts only `aperture`/`shutter`/`iso`, so a persisted `expcomp` survives — the EV readout is misleading but the value is not destroyed. And enforcement is immediate, not "within 3 s": `update()` ends with `reconcile_all(force=True)` rather than waiting for the 3 s loop.

Accurate statement: on any page load the exposure inputs revert to the built-in `DEFAULT_DESIRED` values (f/8, 1/200, ISO 400 — `rigcore.py:353-364`), and the next Apply silently overwrites the fleet's persisted aperture/shutter/ISO with them, with convergence still reporting "synced". Live today this destroys the configured auto-ISO.
fix: On load and after every successful Apply, `GET /api/settings` and populate `#sAp` (`aperture/100`), `#sSh` (low 16 bits of `shutter`), `#sIso`, `#evVal`/`EV` from `expcomp`, and `#sExpMode` from `_auto`. Mark inputs the operator has edited and send only those in the POST, or at minimum diff against the fetched vector so an untouched field is never re-pushed.

title: Run-start calibration frames are pulled into the transect and written to flight_log as survey data; the re-baseline that is supposed to exclude them runs ~15 s too late
goal_clause: "Keep things organized by transect" / "synchronised photogrammetry transects"
failure: Every transect starts with ~6 non-survey exposures per camera (1 USB EXIF-calibration frame + 5 GPIO trigger-latency frames) pulled into the transect folder and written to flight_log as ordinary survey rows, because the re-baseline that is meant to exclude them runs ~13 s late. Two corrections to the reported detail: (1) the _calibrate_exif frame is usually stamped capture_source=gpio_edge via the unscheduled-frame path (run.py:262-270, window=1.0), so it is indistinguishable from a good survey row rather than obviously unsynchronised; (2) only that one concurrently-fired pair could be mistaken for a stereo pair — the 10 calibrate_trigger frames are ~1.2 s apart within a camera and the two cameras' bursts ~6.5 s apart, so they are unpaired singletons. The more damaging consequence the report omits: auto_capture is on by default in the UI (interval 2 s, frames 0) and _start_capture_loop begins firing genuine survey frames ~1 s into the run (run.py:611), so the blanket `for s in w.mon.shots(): w.seen.add(...)` at ~13 s also swallows any real survey frame that has landed on the node but not yet been pulled — those are never pulled, never logged, never retried (seen is added before download) and no event is emitted. Additionally _adopt_loop (run.py:459-460) fires _calibrate_exif for a late-joining camera with no re-baseline at all, so an adopted camera's calibration frame is unconditionally part of the survey.
fix: Have the calibration paths register the frame names they cause. Capture `before = {s["name"] for s in m.shots()}` and, as each calibration frame appears, add its name to the corresponding worker's `seen` set *before* the worker's next poll — or gate the workers (a `paused` Event) until calibration completes and then baseline. Do not rely on a post-hoc bulk re-baseline.

title: One 4-second /health timeout silently drops a camera from the GPIO path to the USB path for the next shots — 0-200 ms skew, no alert
goal_clause: "each image being taken <10ms from eachother" and "Good logic to defensively handle and altert for missing ... cameras"
failure:
Path selection is made from a health dict that is cleared wholesale on ANY single /health failure, with no hysteresis and no alert, so a camera can be silently demoted from the GPIO path (22.1 ms, sd 0.4-0.9 ms) to the USB path (68-76 ms, sd 5-11 ms) while its node stays CAM_CONNECTED and keeps being fired. Against the other camera still on GPIO that is ~50 ms of inter-camera skew (up to the 0-200 ms USB figure in PROTOCOL.md:56), i.e. every affected stereo pair blows the <10 ms requirement. The only trace is `path: "usb"` inside an info-level capture event; the node card's GPIO field does drop to "—" (rig_ui.html:301-303), but there is no anomaly, no warn event, and no run-level record of which frames were USB-fired.

Two corrections to the stated failure mode:

1. The claimed timestamp degradation does not happen in the transient case. The EXPOSURE monitor is a node-side gpiomon that records an edge whenever the body exposes, regardless of how it was triggered, and match_exposure_edge polls /gpio/exposure/events directly with no reference to m.health (run.py:739-790). The USB branch still calls w.note_command(time.time()), and the real exposure lands 68-76 ms later — well inside the 200 ms matching window — so _capture_instant still returns ("gpio_edge", hardware epoch) and the flight_log row keeps a kernel-accurate capture instant. The frames are physically unsynchronised but correctly timestamped, so the damage is detectable post-hoc (the pair's datetime columns diverge by ~50 ms) rather than an unrecoverable corruption of the record. That is the main reason for medium rather than high.

2. The cited trigger — "a Pi 4 too busy to answer /health inside 4 s while streaming frames" — is asserted, not evidenced. piagent is a ThreadingHTTPServer with daemon_threads (piagent.py:957-958), frame pulls go to a different process on :8080, and health() only does GPIO.state() (cheap, no long lock held: fire() busy-waits outside the RLock), IMU.health(), statvfs and one os.listdir. The realistic and more damaging trigger is a piagent that is actually down — crashed, OOM-killed, or restarted for a deploy — while ilxctl keeps the camera claimed: health stays {} indefinitely, EVERY shot of the transect fires over USB, no edges are recorded either (so capture_source really does degrade to exif/command then), and still nothing raises an alert. Same defect, more probable, larger blast radius.

Fix shape: keep a sticky per-node gpio-capability flag that only clears after N consecutive health failures or an explicit "gpio unavailable" reading, add an anomaly for "camera fired on USB / harness unavailable while a run is active", and record the firing path per frame in the flight_log so USB-fired pairs are identifiable in post.
fix: Treat GPIO capability as sticky per node (remember the last successful /gpio/state and only clear it after N consecutive failures), and make a path downgrade loud: if a node that was firing on GPIO takes the USB path, emit a warn event plus a `sync_degraded` anomaly naming the node, and mark those frames in run.json so they can be excluded from photogrammetry.

title: A camera whose trigger-latency calibration produced no samples silently gets zero compensation, giving a 22 ms systematic inter-camera skew
goal_clause: "each image being taken <10ms from eachother, ideally perfectly accurately"
failure: Trigger-latency compensation defaults to zero per node instead of to the fleet median, so a partially-calibrated fleet is far worse than an uncalibrated one. If any connected GPIO node is absent from RunManager.trig_latency, capture_once fires it at `target` while its calibrated peer is fired at `target - 0.0222`, putting the two exposures ~22 ms apart (vs the 0.26 ms body-to-body spread that would result from compensating nobody) for every frame of the transect. The realistic route in is not the ringing EXPOSURE lead — piagent's debounce keeps the first edge of a burst, so cam2 calibrates fine — but calibration coverage: rigd._startup_calibrate (rigd.py:192-211) runs once as soon as a single camera is live and never re-runs, run-start calibration only covers nodes already connected with gpio available, and _adopt_loop (run.py:423-460) gives a mid-run joiner a PullWorker and an EXIF calibration but never calls calibrate_trigger. A camera that boots late or is power-cycled before it was ever calibrated in this rigd process therefore runs the entire transect with zero compensation, with no warning at run start, no per-node calibration state anywhere in rig_ui.html, and both rows correctly reporting capture_source=gpio_edge — the 22 ms is visible only by differencing the two flight_logs after the fact.
fix: Require a measurement for every GPIO-armed connected node: emit an error event and a `calibration_missing` anomaly naming the node when calibrate_trigger returns fewer entries than it had live nodes, refuse to arm the run (or mark it degraded in run.json) rather than defaulting the lead to 0.0, and fall back to the fleet median latency instead of zero. Drop entries for nodes that failed to re-measure instead of keeping stale values.

title: Gpio.fire takes no lock and _LineDriver.shot force-releases FOCUS in its finally block, so overlapping fires drop frames and a held FOCUS becomes a lie that makes triggers silent no-ops
goal_clause: "each image being taken <10ms from eachother" and "Good logic to defensively handle and altert for ... missing data"
failure: _LineDriver.shot() releases FOCUS in its finally (piagent.py:239) without clearing Gpio._focus_direct, and neither Gpio.fire() nor shot() holds Gpio._lock, so FOCUS state changes are not mutually excluded from in-flight shots. This bites only where a FOCUS hold and a lead-fire overlap on one node, which in the shipped app means calibrate_trigger racing the capture loop: run.start() spawns _calibrate_then_reset (run.py:413) and _start_capture_loop (run.py:417) at the same instant, and the UI defaults to auto-capture checked with calibrate=true. The first scheduled shot (focus_lead_ms=120) releases the FOCUS that calibrate_trigger is holding; focus_held() still returns true, so calibrate's remaining no-lead fires pass the guard at piagent.py:418, pulse TRIGGER with FOCUS idle, produce no exposure and no edge, and return ok:true — the run-start per-node trigger-latency measurement silently loses most of its samples (and the surviving samples are separately corrupted by the edge-attribution race at run.py:832), leaving trig_latency stale or wrong for the transect. Symmetrically, calibrate's closing focus hold:false (run.py:836), or a manual /api/capture pressed during an auto-capture run, can drop FOCUS inside a scheduled shot's 120 ms lead and void that single trigger. Survey fires themselves never consult focus_held and always self-assert FOCUS, so this does not cause the dropped frames measured during a sustained 2 fps run, and at interval_s >= ~0.2 s scheduled fire handlers do not overlap on a node at all. Secondary effect: the focus_held field in /gpio/state and the fleet health view is unreliable after any scheduled shot.
fix: Serialize the whole of `fire()` under `self._lock`; have `shot()` capture FOCUS's prior state and restore it rather than forcing IDLE (or set `_focus_direct` to match what it actually leaves behind so `focus_held()` never lies); reject a second /gpio/fire while one is in flight with an explicit busy error so the Jetson can count it; and clamp interval_s to a floor above SYNC_LEAD_S + FOCUS_LEAD_MS.

title: PullWorker._cmds is documented as oldest-first but is appended from concurrent per-node fire threads, so a slow fire reverses two commands and a frame is matched to its neighbour's exposure edge
goal_clause: "Images from each cameras renamed from camera and matched to metadata available at time image was taken"
failure: Requires a /gpio/fire response for one node to be delayed by more than one capture period but less than ~5 s (below the run.py:240-246 age-out), e.g. during the backlog the loop warns about at run.py:634-639. Shot k+1's `note_command` then lands before shot k's, and the two adjacent commands SWAP, not merely displace: frame k arrives, takes `target_{k+1}` as its expected instant and consumes edge k+1; frame k+1 then arrives, finds `target_k` at the head, and consumes the still-buffered edge k (edges live 30 s, run.py:516/778-780). Both frames are written with each other's datetime, filename, nav fix and IMU attitude, one period apart, both labelled capture_source=gpio_edge. The condition self-heals after the pair — it is not a persistent skew, and no frame is lost. The worst consequence for the stated goal is not the ~500 ms geotag error but that `_cmds` is per node: the stalled camera's stream is shifted one shot relative to its partner, so the stereo pair for those two shots is mis-paired by a full period even though inter-camera exposure sync was actually sub-millisecond. Fix is one line — call `note_command(target)` before dispatching the HTTP request on the gpio path, where `t` does not depend on the response at all.
fix: Queue the expected instant from the scheduling loop before dispatching, not from the completion path of each per-node thread; or make `note_command` insert in target order (bisect) rather than append, and have `_capture_instant` select the oldest by value rather than by insertion position.

title: The GPS offset is never applied to any capture stamp, yet the flight_log's time_source column reports 'gps'
goal_clause: "All computers cameras and sensors use gpstime as master clock, falling back to Jetson system time if gps master unavailable"
failure: With the N2K bus powered, PGN 129029 confirmed, and the Jetson RTC drifted (offset must stay under TimeAuthority.MAX_OFFSET_S = 86400 s, or the GPS word is rejected and time_source correctly stays 'jetson'), every flight_log row reports time_source=gps while the `datetime` column and the `CamN_YYYYMMDD_hhmmss.ss` filename are written in raw Jetson time — the correction the column asserts is never applied at the format boundary (_fmt_dt / _fmt_fname, run.py:67-80, called at run.py:200,288). The damage is confined to the absolute UTC label: lat/long/xutm/yutm/depth and every IMU column remain CORRECT, because nav.fix_at() (nav.py:1418-1421) and imu_snapshot() (run.py:711-713) both expect and require a local Jetson-clock epoch, matching against rings keyed by local receive time (nav.py:1220-1225, imu_yb.py:235). Inter-camera skew is also unaffected. The practical harm is that flight_log timestamps cannot be trusted for correlation against any external GPS-time dataset, and the one column that would reveal the discrepancy claims the opposite. A secondary mixed-clock inconsistency exists in the same file: run.py:278 (card-review pulls with no queued command) and the run-id at run.py:362 DO apply gps_offset, so those stamps sit on a different clock from their sibling rows, and the run.py:278 epoch is then passed to nav_snapshot/imu_snapshot as if it were local, mis-matching or blanking nav and IMU for exactly those rows.
fix: In `_write_flight`, latch `off, src = timesync.gps_offset, timesync.source` once, stamp `_fmt_dt(epoch + off)` and pass the same corrected epoch to `_fmt_fname` at run.py:200, and set `time_source = src` from the offset actually applied rather than a second, later `timesync.now()` call. Sample the source at capture time, not at pull time, so a fix acquired between shutter and download cannot relabel an already-captured frame.

title: No node clock is ever verified against the Jetson; /timeprobe is implemented but never called, and piagent.fire() accepts an unbounded absolute at_epoch
goal_clause: "All computers cameras and sensors use gpstime as master clock" / "Good logic to defensively handle and alert for missing sensors or cameras"
failure: No layer ever compares a node's wall clock to the Jetson's, and the timestamps that carry the rig's headline spec are node wall-clock values: piagent publishes epoch_hw = kernel monotonic + (time.time() - time.monotonic()) and run.py's match_exposure_edge now prefers it over the Python stamp. If chrony is dead or was never installed on a node (deploy.sh only configures it in the `provision` path, and every step is `|| true`, so `deploy.sh node camN` alone leaves the Pi on systemd-timesyncd or free-running), the Pi's clock drifts against the Jetson at ordinary crystal rates — roughly 10 ms per 8 minutes at 20 ppm. That offset enters twice: fire() waits to the Jetson-supplied at_epoch on the drifted clock, so the body triggers early or late by exactly the offset, and the EXPOSURE edge is stamped with the same offset, so the flight_log's gpio_edge instant is wrong by it too. Inter-camera skew therefore blows past the 10 ms budget while every row still reads capture_source=gpio_edge, piagent's late_ms reads ~0 (it differences two Pi-clock values), calibrate_trigger's latency reads normal (same reason), and no anomaly fires. Once the offset exceeds the 0.20 s match window the edges stop matching at all and frames fall back to calibrated EXIF — timestamps stay roughly right, but the harness silently stops contributing, again with no alert. The large-offset case (a Pi that comes up minutes behind before chrony's first step) additionally makes fire() sleep inside the handler past the Jetson's 10 s timeout and fire the body minutes later, and because _fire ignores r.get("ok") the Jetson records the shot as dispatched — but that is a narrow boot-window race, self-healing once chrony steps, and it does trip the existing capture-backlog warning.
fix: Poll `/timeprobe` per node on the reconcile loop, store the measured offset, surface it in `/api/diag`, and raise an anomaly (and refuse to start a run) when |offset| exceeds a threshold such as 5 ms. In `piagent.fire()`, reject an `at_epoch` more than a few seconds beyond the node's own clock with an explicit error instead of spinning. In `_fire`, only call `note_command` when the fire reported `ok`.

title: GPS master-clock offset is never applied to image timestamps, and rows in the same CSV mix two clock bases
goal_clause: "All computers cameras and sensors use gpstime as master clock, falling back to Jetson system time if gps master unavailable"
failure: Latent absolute-time-labelling bug, live only once the N2K bus is powered and TimeAuthority confirms a satellite time word. From that moment every filename and every `datetime` cell is raw Jetson local time (GPIO edge, corrected EXIF, and command epoch are all in the Jetson/node chrony timebase) while the `time_source` cell on the same row reads "gps", and the run directory name plus run.json's `started` -- built from timesync.now() at run.py:362 -- are GPS-corrected, so the folder disagrees with the frames and the index epochs inside it. PROTOCOL.md:214-216 promises stamps corrected by gps_offset; they are not. A rare extra consequence: rows that reach the last-resort fallback at run.py:278 carry a GPS-corrected epoch into nav.fix_at() and /imu/window, whose contracts are local epochs, so with |offset| > 3 s (RAPID_STALE_S) or > 0.1 s (IMU_MAX_AGE_S) those specific rows lose lat/long/xutm/yutm and attitude; that path needs an unscheduled frame with no EXPOSURE edge and no measured EXIF offset, so it is uncommon. NOT part of the failure: inter-camera sync and the <10 ms requirement (unaffected -- sync never touches gps_offset), nav/IMU-to-image correlation for normal rows (correct, since frame epochs and the nav history ring share the local timebase), and recoverability -- the offset can be reconstructed in post from nmea_raw.log, which records every 126992/129029 line verbatim against the local wall clock.
fix: Keep raw local epochs for every internal lookup (edge matching, nav ring, IMU window) and apply timesync correction once at the presentation boundary: _fmt_dt(epoch + offset) and _fmt_fname(epoch + offset). Make _capture_instant's fallback return bare time.time() so all four paths share one base. Record gps_offset_s and its source in run.json at run start and stop, and add it to the run's events.log.

title: The "preview on cam1, then deploy to the fleet" workflow does not exist -- every settings change hits all cameras instantly
goal_clause: "Cam1 allows live preview of settings changes before deploying across fleet"
failure: There is no staged/preview settings vector and no per-node exposure route: POST /api/settings (rigd.py:499-500) calls SettingsManager.update() (rigcore.py:428-442), which drops any unrecognised key such as `node`, mutates the one global `desired` map, persists it to DESIRED_PATH, and runs reconcile_all(force=True) across every connected camera inside the same request. The only `node`-aware path, Rig.fanout() (rigd.py:291-304), is wired solely to the focus/zoom endpoints and the UI never populates it. A per-node change made out-of-band directly against a node's ilxctl would be reverted within 3 s by Rig._reconcile_loop (rigd.py:212-218). Consequence: to evaluate a new exposure the operator must commit both bodies to it and destructively overwrite the saved survey configuration with no retained prior value to undo to; evaluation happens only after the fact via cam1's live view and histogram. Both bodies stay mutually consistent, so mid-run stereo pairs are not mismatched — the harm is workflow friction plus a lost/unrecoverable prior configuration, and a documentation contract violation: PROTOCOL.md:16 and HANDOFF.md:13 both state cam1 performs exposure preview, a role no code implements.
fix: Add a staged vector: POST /api/settings/preview {..} applies the pending values to cam1 (the primary) only, leaves `desired` untouched, and marks cam1 as intentionally-diverged so the reconcile loop does not yank it back; POST /api/settings/commit promotes the staged vector into `desired` and fans out; POST /api/settings/revert re-converges cam1. In the UI, split "Apply to fleet" into "Preview on Cam1" and "Deploy to fleet", with the pending-vs-live diff shown next to cam1's live view and histogram.

title: Push failures for fields with no readback key are collected into a dead variable and excluded from the convergence badge
goal_clause: "Good logic to defensively handle and alert for missing sensors or cameras or missing data" / "Settings are adjusted then applied to all cameras"
failure: Push failures for the four fields with no readback key (filetype, imagesize, transsize at rigcore.py:347-349, and expcomp) are appended to the dead local `diverged` (rigcore.py:468, 509/514/524) and dropped: no event is emitted, nothing enters m.convergence["diverged"], and because Camera::setExposure never calls log() and fail() never touches the log ring, the rejection does not even appear in the ilxctl log tail carried in /api/status. The realistic trigger is a user Apply (update() -> reconcile_all(force=True)) against a body whose FileType property is momentarily non-writable -- on its menu, or PC-remote control priority lost -- while aperture/shutter/iso/drive already match desired, so the post-push verification read (540-545) finds `still` empty, publishes synced:true, and the Fleet card (rig_ui.html:283-286) and Controls strip (574-581) both show a green "synced" dot while cam2 is still at the previous or factory file type/size. The rejected field is silently re-pushed every 3 s by _reconcile_loop (rigd.py:214-217), so transient locks clear on their own; the persistent case shoots a transect at mismatched filetype/imagesize/transsize between the two bodies -- differing resolution and format in a stereo pair, degrading photogrammetry -- with no alert ever raised. A distinct and more damaging variant sits in the same three lines: the `elif not key: pushed[field] = target` at 515-516 is also reached when the POST times out (`_unreachable: True`), recording an unsent push as applied in m._pushed, which does NOT self-heal on the next pass because the blind field is then skipped until a force or a readable-field revert clears the cache.
fix: Fold `diverged` into the published state: `still = still + [f for f in diverged if f not in still]`, and emit settings_divergent for blind-field push failures with the ilxctl error text attached, so a setting that cannot be applied is visible in exactly the same place as a readable one.

title: UI shutter encoder hardcodes numerator 1, so no exposure of 1 s or longer can be expressed
goal_clause: "Settings are adjusted then applied to all cameras" (usable exposure control in the field)
failure: The fleet exposure panel can only ever express 1/N shutter speeds: rig_ui.html:561 freezes the numerator at 1 in the (num<<16)|den encoding. Exposures longer than 1 s (2", 4", 30" = (2<<16)|1, (4<<16)|1, (30<<16)|1) and every non-unit-numerator speed the body offers (1.3", 2.5", ...) are unreachable from the UI; 1 s itself is reachable by typing 1 (1/1 = 65537). Because the reconcile loop (rigd.py:214-219) re-pushes desired["shutter"] every 3 s, setting a long exposure on the body or through the per-camera ilxctl UI at :8080 is reverted within one cycle, so the only workaround is hand-editing ~/rig/desired.json - and that is clobbered the next time anyone presses "Apply to fleet", since the panel's fields are never populated from the current desired vector and always re-send f/8, 1/200, ISO 400. Separately, the same line has no bounds: an empty field yields +'' === 0 and pushes 1/0 (enc 65536), and a value above 65535 ORs into the numerator bits (70000 -> num 1, den 4464). Those values are not on the body's shutter list, so setProp (src/camera.cpp:677-709) fails or the read-back check at rigcore.py:536-556 catches it - the camera keeps its previous shutter rather than shooting a different one silently, but the fleet is left permanently non-converged with a settings_divergent warn re-emitted every 3 s indefinitely, the exact alarm-fatigue pattern the surrounding code elsewhere goes out of its way to avoid.
fix: Replace the free-form 1/N box with a <select> populated from the primary camera's `shutterChoices` (camera.cpp:1628 already emits {v,l} pairs with correct labels), so every speed the body supports -- including multi-second exposures -- is selectable and no value outside the body's legal set can be sent.

title: The goal's "Cam1 previews settings changes before deploying across the fleet" workflow does not exist — every exposure change goes to all cameras at once
goal_clause: "Cam1 allows live preview of settings changes before deploying across fleet"
failure: There is no way to drive cam1's exposure alone: every exposure change commits the fleet-wide `desired` vector (rigcore.py:428-441), persists it to disk, and force-reconciles every connected camera, so the operator cannot try a setting on the primary and then decide whether to deploy it -- the "try, then deploy" gate the goal statement and docs/PROTOCOL.md:16 both promise does not exist. The consequence is operational friction and a documented-contract violation, not lost imagery: Apply only writes device properties and never captures, so frames are affected only if an auto-capture run is concurrently firing, and in that case both bodies move together and stay radiometrically matched (which is what stereo photogrammetry needs -- a cam1-only preview mid-run would produce mismatched pairs and be worse). The operator is also not left guessing: the Controls tab already shows per-camera live view, the per-camera aperture/shutter/ISO readout (rig_ui.html:611), and a live histogram with mean/range/clip bound to the primary (rig_ui.html:622-638), so the result of a change is visible within about a second and is revertible with a second Apply.
fix: Add a preview path: `POST /api/settings/preview {node:'cam1', aperture, shutter, iso}` in rigd that fans the exposure fields to that one node's ilxctl `/api/exposure` and marks the node preview-pinned so SettingsManager._reconcile_node skips it (otherwise the 3 s reconcile reverts the preview). In the UI, split the button into "Preview on Cam1" and "Apply to fleet", show a PREVIEW badge on the cam1 live-view column with the pending values and the histogram bound to it, and have "Apply to fleet" promote the previewed vector into `desired` and clear the pin. Add a timeout/cancel that unpins and reverts cam1 so a forgotten preview cannot desynchronise the pair into a run.

title: Anomalies are rendered only while the Controls tab is open; there is no global alert surface during a run
goal_clause: "Good logic to defensively handle and alert for missing sensors or cameras or missing data"
failure: The anomaly surface is not merely unrendered off the Controls tab — for several detectors it is never computed. Anomalies.scan() (rigd.py:50) is called from only two places, /api/anomalies (rigd.py:432) and /api/diag (rigd.py:430); nothing in the repo polls /api/diag and there is no background scan thread, so scan() runs only while a browser sits on Controls. Detectors with no independent emitter — battery_low (rigd.py:78), disk_low (rigd.py:84), jitter_high (rigd.py:124), camera_absent (rigd.py:65), nav_gateway_down (rigd.py:107) — are therefore never evaluated, the `self.events.emit("warn", ...)` at rigd.py:140 never fires for them, and they do not appear in the Events tab backlog either. Detectors that duplicate an independent emitter — pull_fail (run.py:175/184/193/206), imu_stall (run.py:732), settings_divergent (rigcore.py:569), node_offline via node_transition (rigcore.py:244) — do reach the events ring, and pollEvents runs ungated every 2 s (rig_ui.html:702), so those are recoverable by switching to the Events tab after the fact. Corrected concrete case: 12 minutes into a transect, cam2 drops to 8% battery and its pulls start failing. rigd never detects battery_low at all (no client on Controls, so no scan); the pull_fail warns do land in the event ring but render only inside the hidden #tab-events list. The operator on Review sees no colour change, count, or sound; header pills hRun/hNodes/hTime are unaffected because cam2 is still connected, and hNav is stuck at its default because it is only written by the Nav-tab-gated pollNav().
fix: Poll `/api/anomalies` on its own interval independent of TAB, add a header pill showing the highest-severity firing anomaly and a count (red for offline/fail kinds, amber otherwise) that is clickable to the Controls/Anomalies panel, and flash the tab strip when a new anomaly kind appears. Also mirror `warn`+ events into a persistent toast so a fault that clears is still noticed.

title: Nothing compares shots fired against frames pulled, and a failed GPIO fire is never inspected — a camera that stops delivering raises no alert at all
goal_clause: "Good logic to defensively handle and alert for ... missing data"
failure: Narrower than claimed: a node that remains CAM_CONNECTED and settings-converged but stops delivering new frames (body PC-save/priority lost, card/USB stall, shutter refused) is never alarmed. capture_once ignores the /gpio/fire reply's ok/error (run.py:577), the auto-capture loop discards the whole result (run.py:628-632), and nothing compares commands issued against frames pulled: Anomalies.scan (rigd.py:121-135) only checks interval_jitter_ms>120 and failed>2, where `failed` counts download/truncation/write errors in _handle, never absent frames. _capture_instant even recognises the miss and silently discards the aged command (run.py:240-246). The result is no anomaly, no event above debug, and a stale last_capture nobody inspects — though the condition is visible unalarmed in the fleet UI's per-node "Run pull: N ok / M fail" counter, and the common causes with a status signature (node offline, camera unclaimed, store_dest reverted, pull failures, low disk) are still caught by existing detectors. Three of the four piagent ok:False cases the claim cites cannot occur on this path at all.
fix: Count fires per node in the RunManager (the command deque already tracks them — a command aged out at run.py:240-246 is a fire that produced no frame) and add two detectors to Anomalies.scan: (a) `fire_failed` when a /gpio/fire reply is not ok, and (b) `frames_missing` when fired-minus-pulled exceeds a small threshold, or when one node of the pair has pulled >20% fewer frames than another. Escalate to error severity, since this is the failure that silently voids a survey.

title: A frame is marked seen before it is downloaded, so a failed pull is never retried and the image is lost permanently
goal_clause: "Images from each cameras renamed from camera and matched to metadata" — the survey data itself
failure: A frame is added to `seen` before the pull is attempted (run.py:167), so any failure inside `_handle` permanently removes that frame from the survey — no poll ever looks at the name again. The reachable trigger is NOT a link outage (a dead node yields `shots() == []` and an OFFLINE gate at run.py:161, so nothing is marked seen and everything is pulled once the link returns); it is any failure where the LISTING succeeds and the transfer or local write does not: (1) a partially-written PC-save file — `shotsJson()` in src/main.cpp:70-90 stats and lists whatever is in the save dir with no completeness test, and `/shot/` serves it byte-for-byte, so a frame caught mid-write is rejected by the Content-Length or SOI/EOI check and is then permanently skipped even though the complete file is on the node milliseconds later; (2) a degraded (not dead) link where the small `/api/shots` GET succeeds while the multi-hundred-KB `/shot/` transfer times out at 30 s or is reset; (3) local write errors — a full or read-only Jetson disk means every remaining frame of the transect is skipped forever, even after space is freed. In each case the frame is absent from the run folder, from flight_log.csv and from run.json, and its nav/IMU-at-capture row can never be reconstructed exactly, although the JPEG itself survives on both the camera card and the node's PC-save dir and the failing filename is journalled in the run's events.log, so manual recovery is possible.
fix: Only add to `seen` after a successful write; on failure record the name in a retry set with an attempt counter and re-attempt on subsequent polls (bounded, e.g. 5 tries with backoff), emitting an error and giving up only after the bound. The node's save dir is never pruned, so the bytes are still there — the retry costs nothing but a second GET.

title: GPIO harness health is never alarmed, and one piagent timeout silently downgrades a camera to unsynchronised USB firing mid-run
goal_clause: "each image being taken <10ms from eachother" + "alert for missing sensors"
failure: The trigger path is chosen per shot at run.py:567 from a health dict that rigcore.py:276 blanks wholesale on one failed /health poll, and because OFFLINE requires both ilxctl and piagent to be unreachable, a piagent-only fault leaves the node CAM_CONNECTED and firing over USB. The degradation lasts at least one 2 s poll cycle (so several shots at 2 fps, not just "the very next shot"), and persists indefinitely if piagent crashes or restarts while ilxctl stays up — that camera is then unscheduled for the rest of the transect and, since /gpio/exposure/events also fails, its rows fall back to EXIF (whole-second DateTimeOriginal plus calibrated offset) instead of kernel edge stamps. In the transient case the frame usually still matches its true EXPOSURE edge within the 0.20 s window (run.py:739), so the flight_log keeps accurate instants and the physical desync is recoverable in post; the harm is the lost sub-millisecond synchrony, not falsified metadata. Separately and more solidly, no runtime layer alarms on any harness field: Anomalies.scan never inspects h["gpio"], so a dead EXPOSURE lead (monitor_running true, edges_seen frozen at 0) and harness_safe:false / inputs_parked:false — the permanent half-press state that docs/harness-and-strobe.md:110 says must be treated as an operator-visible fault — raise nothing, and rig_ui.html:301-303 does not render those fields at all.
fix: Add a `gpio_degraded` detector to Anomalies.scan covering available:false, monitor_running:false, harness_safe:false/inputs_parked:false, and edges_bounced/edges_seen above a ratio threshold. In capture_once, treat a missing/blank health dict as 'unknown, do not silently downgrade': keep the last known-good gpio availability per node, and if a node genuinely has no harness during an active run, emit a warn per shot and mark those flight_log rows so the skew is visible in the data, not just inferable.

title: Run IDs are minute-resolution, so restarting a transect within the same minute merges two surveys into one directory and destroys the first run.json
goal_clause: "Keep things organized by transect"
failure: Two runs started in the same UTC minute with the same label resolve to the same run_id and the same directory under ~/rig-runs. Nothing is lost from the survey itself: _uniq_dest (run.py:83-100) prevents any image overwrite so the directory holds the complete union; flight_log.csv, events.log and nmea_raw.log are all appended, with navlog's per-session open/close records (navlog.py:114-121) and the "run started"/"run stopped" events making the boundary recoverable. The real damage is that run 2's _write_run_json() at run.py:403 fires before any frame arrives and os.replace (run.py:926) atomically destroys run 1's run.json — permanently dropping run 1's per-frame index, its renamed->original camera filename mapping (the only copy: FLIGHT_HEADER at run.py:29-33 has no original-name column), its node list, start time and config. The surviving run.json then reports only run 2's frame count while the directory contains both runs' images and interleaved CSV rows, so the manifest silently under-reports the transect on disk.
fix: Include seconds in the run_id, or detect the collision in start() and refuse/suffix: if os.path.exists(root), append '_b', '_c', … and log it. Never open an existing run root with exist_ok=True.

title: Two runs started in the same minute with the same label silently merge into one transect directory, and the first run's run.json is destroyed
goal_clause: "Keep things organized by transect" / "saved as csv flight_log"
failure: Two runs started in the same UTC minute with the same label (the shipped UI default "transect-01" never auto-increments) resolve to the same run_id and share one directory, with no warning in the API response or the UI. Realistic trigger is a false start: Start, notice cam2 is not converged, Stop, fix, Start again inside 60 s; also a rigd restart mid-transect followed by a restart within the same minute. Consequences: (a) both sessions' frames sit in the same cam1/cam2 folders and their rows are appended into one flight_log.csv under a single header with no separator, so the aborted start's frames are silently absorbed into the survey; (b) _write_run_json (run.py:403) unconditionally os.replaces run.json at start, so the first session's per-frame index is dropped and the finished run.json describes only the last session - the manifest's `frames` count and index under-report the directory's actual contents, the exact inconsistency stop() at run.py:477-482 is written to prevent. This violates the "keep things organized by transect" requirement. It is NOT unrecoverable data destruction: no image is overwritten (_uniq_dest), no flight_log row is lost, the fname->original-camera-name mapping survives in ~/rig/rigd.jsonl via the per-frame debug event, and nmea_raw.log carries explicit per-session "# open run_id=" / "# close" markers delimiting the two sessions.
fix: Refuse to reuse an existing run root: after building `rid`, loop appending `_a`, `_b`… (or a seconds field / monotonic counter) until `os.mkdir(root)` succeeds without EEXIST, and return the actual run_id. Never open the run root with exist_ok=True. Additionally make PullWorker refuse to append to a flight_log.csv it did not create.

title: A frame is added to `seen` before it is successfully pulled, so any transient or partial-read failure loses that survey image permanently with no flight_log row
goal_clause: "Good logic to defensively handle and alert for … missing data" / "Images from each camera … matched to metadata"
failure: There is no bounded retry for a frame whose pull fails: run.py:167 adds the name to `seen` before `_handle` runs, and nothing in the codebase ever removes it or re-scans. The reachable trigger is NOT a partial-write/size-mismatch race (measured non-existent: 24/24 frames at 2 fps on both a Pi5 and a Pi4 pulled byte-exact, and /api/shots sampled at ~3 ms never once showed a frame at an intermediate size). It is a genuine transient transport fault — an Ethernet blip, or a node rebooting mid-run, which on this rig happens whenever a body is power-cycled because the shared PoE feed reboots its Pi. Such a frame gets no rename and no flight_log row for the remainder of the run, and its stereo mate on the other camera is left unpaired; a re-adopted worker re-baselines it as "old" (run.py:145-146), so re-adoption does not recover it either. The JPEG itself is not destroyed — store_dest=3 (PC + card, verified live) keeps a copy on the camera's SD card, and nothing deletes it from the node's save dir, where /shot/<name> and the UI shot browser still serve it — so recovery is manual and after the fact rather than impossible. Operator signal is only a pull_fail anomaly once failed > 2 (rig/rigd.py:131-135).
fix: Only mark a name seen once `_handle` reports success. Keep a bounded `pending` dict of name→attempts and retry on the next poll (with a short backoff), dropping to a hard failure — and a flight_log-visible gap record — only after N attempts. For the mid-write case specifically, require the same st_size on two consecutive polls (or have ilxctl write to `name.part` and rename) before pulling.

title: The post-calibration bulk re-baseline marks every frame currently on the node as 'already seen', silently discarding real survey frames fired by the auto-capture loop during calibration
goal_clause: "Good logic to defensively handle and alert for … missing data"
failure:
At rig/run.py:857-862 (HEAD 672-676), `_calibrate_then_reset` blanket-marks the node's entire save dir as seen after ~13 s of calibration during which the auto-capture loop has been firing survey frames. Because `_poll_once` (run.py:167) adds a name to `seen` before downloading it, the loss is confined to frames that appeared in the Pi's save dir after the worker's last 0.4 s poll and before the re-baseline's `shots()` call: realistically 0-1 survey frames per camera per run, dropped with no flight_log row, no `failed` increment, and no event — `run["alerts"]` (run.py:388) is never populated and nothing reconciles shots fired against frames pulled.

The same line is also wrong in the opposite direction, which the claim does not state: the re-baseline is far too LATE for its own documented purpose. The PullWorker polls every 0.4 s throughout calibration, so calibration's own 5 fires per camera are downloaded, renamed, given nav/IMU snapshots and written into flight_log.csv as survey rows long before line 857 executes. Worse, a calibration frame arriving while an auto-capture command sits at the head of `_cmds` can satisfy `_capture_instant`'s edge match (run.py:229-239, ±200 ms window) and consume that command plus its edge, so a calibration exposure is logged with a scheduled survey shot's timestamp and the command queue is left shifted by one. So the net effect of the current design is: calibration frames reliably enter the survey, while real survey frames are occasionally and silently removed from it.

The clean fix is to not overlap the two at all — hold `_start_capture_loop` until `_calibrate_then_reset` has finished — and to make the re-baseline a diff against a snapshot of `shots()` taken before `calibrate_trigger()` rather than a blanket over everything present after it.
fix: Never bulk-baseline while a run can be producing frames. Track calibration-caused filenames explicitly (see the previous finding) and exclude only those, or hold the auto-capture loop until `_calibrate_then_reset` has completed and only then start firing.

title: _calibrate_exif measures the camera clock against a USB shutter command instead of the GPIO exposure edge, biasing every capture_source=exif timestamp early by the dispatch latency
goal_clause: "each image being taken <10ms from eachother" / "matched to metadata available at time image was taken"
failure: _calibrate_exif implements only the FALLBACK half of PROTOCOL.md:217-218 ("else command epoch + 20 ms"; the code uses 24 ms, adding the 4.5 ms curtain) and never the preferred "diff vs GPIO exposure edge when available", despite the edge being available at calibration time (a USB-fired exposure drives the same EXPOSURE line, and match_exposure_edge() already exists). Because t_cmd is sampled before the blocking HTTP-to-ilxctl-to-SDK dispatch, exif_offset absorbs that dispatch latency, so every capture_source=exif row's datetime and filename are early by it, per node and therefore differentially between cameras. Impact is confined to the exif fallback branch, which is reached only when the harness produces no edge for that frame -- not the case on either live node today, where debouncing works and edges are flowing. On that branch the camera clock's own quantization (whole-second DateTimeOriginal when SubSec is absent) is the dominant error term, and the row is already labelled capture_source=exif, so the degradation is recorded rather than silent. Real spec deviation and worth fixing by calibrating against the edge, but it is a fallback-path accuracy refinement, not a survey-corrupting defect.
fix: In `_calibrate_exif`, when the node has a working harness, fire via `/gpio/fire` and use the resulting EXPOSURE fall edge as `true_epoch` (as PROTOCOL.md requires); on the USB fallback, derive `true_epoch` from the shutter response's own completion time minus the SDK's release lag rather than from the pre-call `t_cmd`, and record the residual uncertainty into `time_err_ms`.

title: Run-start calibration frames are pulled and written into the transect's flight_log as survey rows
goal_clause: "Keep things organized by transect" + "matched to metadata available at time image was taken"
failure: Every run start silently adds ~6 non-survey images and ~6 flight_log rows per camera to the transect: one from _calibrate_exif's m.shutter() and five from calibrate_trigger's /gpio/fire, all pulled by the already-running PullWorkers during the ~14s calibration window, before _calibrate_then_reset re-baselines w.seen (which consequently only catches frames still in transit, making the guard its docstring promises ineffective). The rows are not mis-stamped -- branch 2a of _capture_instant matches each frame to its own EXPOSURE edge, so capture_source=gpio_edge and nav/IMU are correct for the true capture instant. The defect is contamination, not corruption: the transect gains redundant frames shot from the stationary start-of-line position, they belong to no synchronized stereo pair (calibrate_trigger walks the nodes sequentially, so cam1's and cam2's calibration exposures are ~7s apart), frame counts and per-worker stats in run.json are inflated, and no column distinguishes them from survey exposures. A separate consequence of the same re-baseline, worth noting but not claimed: with auto_capture enabled the capture loop runs concurrently with calibration, so the w.seen.add() sweep at run.py:857-862 can also mark genuine survey frames that landed but were not yet polled as already-seen, dropping them from the log entirely.
fix: Mark calibration frames explicitly: snapshot the camera's shot list before calibrating and add those names to each worker's `seen` set BEFORE firing, or hold the workers in a paused state until _calibrate_then_reset completes.

title: The Controls focus-mode selector is reverted by the convergence loop within 3 s while the UI keeps showing the operator's choice
goal_clause: "UI is intuitive, easy to use" / "Settings are adjusted then applied to all cameras"
failure: The Controls focus-mode selector never sticks and the UI never reveals it. Operator picks AF-S (or DMF) in #fMode; the fanout applies it to both bodies, but within ~1-6 s (2 s status poll + 3 s reconcile, or instantly on any Apply/EV bump which calls reconcile_all(force=True)) rigcore.py:527-530 pushes focus_mode=1 (MF) back to every camera. The select keeps showing the operator's stale choice forever (ctlChoicesLoaded latch + fillSel's dataset.n early return), focusModeLabel is never rendered, and focus_mode is not in CONVERGE_FIELDS so it never appears in the convergence/divergence badge. The practical loss is not "AF never completes" - no capture path ever requests AF (all pass af=False) - but that a documented rig-wide control is unusable and the UI lies about the fleet's state: a deliberate one-off AF acquire via the GPIO half-press (/api/node/focus) becomes a no-op once the mode has snapped back to MF, with nothing in the UI or event log to say why. Additionally, because focus_mode bypasses the m._pushed blind-field cache and its result is unchecked, a body that never reports focusMode==1 gets a redundant SetDeviceProperty write every 3 s, silently.
fix: Route /api/focus/mode through SettingsManager.update({'focus_mode': m}) so the user's choice becomes the desired value instead of being fought by it, and re-render #fMode from the primary's live `focusMode` on each Controls poll rather than latching it once.

title: No validation of the settings vector: a cleared field persists a value no body will accept, permanently unconverging that setting
goal_clause: "Good logic to defensively handle and alert for missing sensors or cameras or missing data"
failure: An operator clears the ISO (or aperture/shutter) number box in rig_ui.html and clicks Apply. The inputs have no min/validation and are never repopulated from server state, so `+'' === 0` sends iso:0 (aperture:0, or shutter 1/0). SettingsManager.update() (rigcore.py:428-440) filters keys but not values and persists to ~/rig/desired.json; _load() merges by key with no value check, so the bad value survives every rigd restart. Nothing downstream validates - rigd forwards the raw JSON, ilxctl's /api/exposure only magnitude-clamps (main.cpp:449), and Camera::setPropLocked (camera.cpp:677) checks the enable flag but never the body's enumerated choice list. ISO 0 is not a valid alias (CrISO_AUTO is 0xFFFFFF), so the body never takes it and readback never equals the target: _reconcile_node re-issues the write to both cameras every 3 s indefinitely and, past two strikes, emits a settings_divergent warning per camera per cycle into the unrotated ~/rig/rigd.jsonl. The under-reported amplification: because the diverged field is a *readable* one, the `reverted` check at rigcore.py:485-491 fires on every pass and clears m._pushed, defeating the blind-field cache so filetype/imagesize/transsize/expcomp are ALSO re-pushed every 3 s - restoring the exact multi-write-per-camera USB storm that cache was added to prevent, on the same USB link frame pulls contend for during a live transect. Mitigating: both bodies reject the write identically so the stereo pair stays matched and no imagery is corrupted; the condition is surfaced clearly as a single deduplicated /api/anomalies entry naming the field and a red per-camera badge in the convergence panel; and recovery is in-band (retype the value and Apply, or read the bad vector from /api/diag) - no SSH required. The residual diagnostic cost is that the anomaly's suggested_action points at the camera body ("check the field is settable in the current exposure mode; inspect ilxctl log") rather than at the invalid desired value.
fix: Validate in SettingsManager.update(): reject None and out-of-range values, and where the primary's status offers a choice list (isoChoices/shutterChoices/apertureChoices/driveChoices) reject anything not in it, returning the rejection in the POST response so the UI can show it. Add a rate limit / backoff to the settings_divergent emitter so an unattainable target alarms once per state change, not every 3 s.

title: There is no transect browser anywhere in the UI — the operator can never see the renamed frames, the flight_log, or any past run
goal_clause: "Images from each camera renamed ... saved as csv flight_log ... Keep things organized by transect"
failure: There is no post-hoc run browser: rigd serves no /api/runs listing, no run.json reader and no file route out of ~/rig-runs, so past transects cannot be reopened and flight_log.csv cannot be downloaded from the app. In-run verification is present (run root echoed on start, per-node pulled/failed counters, run frame count, and per-frame renamed-name debug events), but it is transient: once RunManager.stop() clears self.active, status() returns {"active": False}, the Fleet cards' pull counters blank and the header reverts to "no run", and rig_ui.html:571 discards the per-node summary that /api/run/stop returns, printing only "stopped <rid>". So after a run ends the operator's only in-app record is the debug event ring (5000 entries, i.e. the tail of a long transect), and retrieving the CSV or the renamed files still requires SSH.
fix: Add `GET /api/runs` (list `~/rig-runs` with run.json summary: label, start, nodes, frames/camera), `GET /api/run/<rid>` (run.json + per-camera flight_log row count + pair-completeness), `GET /api/run/<rid>/frame?cam=&name=` and `GET /api/run/<rid>/flight_log.csv?cam=` in rigd.Handler.do_GET, all path-validated against RUNS_DIR. Then add a Transects tab (or a run selector on Review) that lists runs newest-first and, when a run is selected, drives the existing side-by-side Review columns off the run's renamed frames and flight_log instead of `/api/shots`, showing lat/lon/pitch/roll/capture_source per frame from the CSV row. Keep `/api/shots` only as the "live spool" mode.

title: The IMU tab's only troubleshooting instruction sends the operator to cam3, a node with no hardware; the IMU is on cam1
goal_clause: "UI is intuitive, easy to use" / "alert for missing sensors"
failure: Stale hardcoded node name in a warning string. Because rigd._imu_host() discovers the IMU node across the whole fleet, this badge renders only when NO node is serving IMU samples — i.e. during a genuine IMU outage, never while cam1 is sampling. In that outage the app's one remediation hint misdirects the operator to cam3, a slot with no Pi at all, and implies cam3 is the Pi 5 when cam1 is. Cost is confused field-troubleshooting minutes; the correct node is still shown on the Fleet tab's per-node IMU row, in the live badge's node label, and in imu_stall alerts, which are tagged with the real node name. It does not compound with empty flight_log IMU columns: run.py no longer pins imu_node="cam3" (now None with fleet discovery), and the IMU tab never consulted that field in the first place.
fix: Replace the hard-coded node name with the discovered one. rigd._imu_host() (rigd.py:306-322) already probes every node and returns the answer as `w.node`; have `/api/imu/window` return the last-probed node name (and the list of nodes probed) even when `present:false`, and render "no IMU found on cam1, cam2 — check the YB-MRA02 USB-A connection on the node that carries it". Never name a node the code has not just probed.

title: "Capture one" reports success by name even when every camera's fire failed
goal_clause: "alert for ... missing data"
failure: The UI does render an affirmative "captured: cam1, cam2" for a fire that every node rejected, but the reachable triggers are far narrower than claimed. There is no arm/disarm state (GPIO.available = _HAVE_GPIO is fixed for the piagent process, piagent.py:293); a stale target epoch is not rejected but fires immediately with ok:True and a late_ms field (piagent.py:426-433, 448-454); and "trigger line unavailable" cannot occur on the live gpiod path, since _LineDriver.shot() returns None only when a line handle is missing, which implies driver.ok is False and that branch is not taken (piagent.py:215-228, 435-447). The realistic triggers are an HTTP 500 from an exception inside GPIO.fire, or a fire dispatched in the sub-2s window between piagent dying and NodeMonitor._tick clearing m.health (rigcore.py:271-276) so the unreachable stub lands in results. There is also a related and more reachable blindness the claim missed: the UI discards results[node]["path"] as well, so once health is cleared, has_gpio goes false and _fire silently drops to the unsynchronised USB path (10-80 ms inter-camera spread) — which renders identically to a GPIO-scheduled stereo pair. Separately, even a fully successful GPIO reply only proves a wire was pulsed, not that the body exposed a frame, so a per-node ok check alone would not make "captured" trustworthy.
fix: Have the UI inspect each entry: report `ok` nodes and failed nodes separately with the error string ("cam1 ok · cam2 FAILED: gpio busy"), and colour the line red on any failure. In run.py, set the top-level `ok` to False when no node's fire succeeded, and include a per-node `ok` boolean so the UI is not parsing heterogeneous piagent payloads.

title: Nothing anywhere measures free space on the Jetson volume where every transect is actually written
goal_clause: "Good logic to defensively handle and alert for ... missing data"
failure: There is no preflight or in-run capacity check on the Jetson volume that holds ~/rig-runs; the disk_low detector (rigd.py:83) and the Fleet "Disk" field (rig_ui.html:306) both report only the Pi's PC-save spool (piagent.py:844). If the Jetson root does fill, the condition is caught reactively rather than silently: each failed `open(dest,'wb')`/write raises OSError at run.py:202-203, increments `failed`, and emits an error-severity `pull_fail` event carrying the literal "[Errno 28] No space left on device" text, which the UI polls unconditionally every 2 s (rig_ui.html:702) into the Events tab, plus a `pull_fail` anomaly once failed > 2 (rigd.py:133-136). The imagery itself is not destroyed — neither piagent nor ilxctl ever deletes a served frame (src/main.cpp:459-500), so originals remain in the Pi's save dir. The real losses are (a) no advance warning before writes start failing, and (b) no retry: `self.seen.add(name)` runs before `_handle` (run.py:166-168), so frames that failed during the full-disk window are never re-pulled even after space is freed, leaving them with no flight_log row and therefore no nav/IMU correlation.
fix: Add `os.statvfs(RUNS_DIR)` to `Rig.diag()`/`Rig.fleet()` as `jetson_free_mb`, add a `runs_disk_low` anomaly with a threshold sized to the expected run (frames × interval × mean frame size), display it in the header and in the pre-flight check, and refuse (or loudly warn on) a run start when the projected run will not fit.

title: Review and Controls rebuild their camera columns only when the connected-camera COUNT changes, so a same-poll swap leaves the wrong camera's frames on screen
goal_clause: "UI is intuitive, easy to use" (and PROTOCOL.md:196-197 "dynamically adds/removes camera columns as nodes come and go")
failure: If the set of connected cameras changes membership without changing count inside a single 2 s poll (one camera's claim comes up in the same window another's is lost -- only the REACHABLE-but-unclaimed transition, since a fully OFFLINE node keeps reporting connected:true from rigcore's stale status cache), renderReviewHeaders/renderCtlLive skip the rebuild. Review then throws a TypeError at rig_ui.html:344 (and 369) on the missing `#exp-<name>`/`#burn-<name>` elements, so the Review tab keeps showing the departed camera's column -- correctly labelled with that camera's own name -- while the newly-live camera has no column at all; Controls degrades silently via its null guards (611, 614), leaving the departed camera's last live-view frame and a frozen histogram (drawHist is never re-invoked, since histPrimary is no longer in the connected list) under that camera's name. The state clears automatically on the next change in connected count, and the Fleet cards plus the #hNodes pill remain accurate throughout, so the operator retains a correct status surface.
fix: Key the rebuild on the identity of the connected set (e.g. `live.map(n=>n.name).join(',')`) rather than its length, in both renderReviewHeaders and renderCtlLive; null-guard the per-node lookups at lines 344 and 369; and stamp each live-view image with the age of its last successful load so a frozen frame is visibly stale rather than passing as current.

title: stop() closes the per-run events.log before detaching it, and EventLog.emit only guards OSError — a concurrent emit raises ValueError and kills that thread for the rest of the session
goal_clause: "defensively handle and alert for missing sensors or cameras" — a dead NodeMonitor stops all camera-loss detection
failure: stop() closes the per-run events.log at run.py:496 but only detaches it from the EventLog at run.py:501, and the close is not serialised against EventLog._lock, so any emit landing in the ~1 ms window (or concurrent with the close itself) hits `self._run_fh.write()` on a closed file and raises ValueError, which emit's `except OSError` does not catch. In practice the threads most likely to be in that window are the auto-capture loop's final emit (run.py:643) and an in-flight capture_once's emit (run.py:600), both of which are the last useful statement of a thread that was exiting anyway, so the usual observable consequence is a stray "Exception in thread" traceback on stderr and a lost final capture event. The severe outcome the claim describes - a NodeMonitor or the reconcile loop dying permanently, freezing that node's state/health/convergence and silently disabling auto-reconnect with no alert (no thread supervision, no age_s in the UI) - is mechanically possible via the nested re-emitting handlers (rigcore.py:262-268, rigcore.py:455-462, rigd.py:214-220) but requires a node state transition or a reconcile error to coincide with a sub-millisecond window that opens once per transect stop; both of those emitters are completely silent in the measured steady state.
fix: Reverse the order — self.events.set_run_file(None) first, then close the handles — and broaden the guard in EventLog.emit to `except (OSError, ValueError)` for both the jsonl and the run-file writes. Better still, have set_run_file(None) do the close itself under the EventLog lock so the two can never be observed out of step.

title: rigd shutdown or crash never finalises an active run, and there is no recovery on restart
goal_clause: "Keep things organized by transect" + defensive handling of missing data
failure: rigd has no SIGTERM/atexit finalisation and no restart-time recovery, so an abnormal exit mid-transect leaves the run un-finalised. The concrete loss is confined to run.json bookkeeping: `final` stays false, `frames`/`index` are stale by up to 9 entries (run.py:908-910 rewrites only every 10th frame), and the per-worker `stats` summary is never written. Images, per-frame flight_log.csv rows and events.log lines are all flushed as they are produced and survive intact, so the survey deliverable itself is not damaged. The one genuine data-quality consequence, not stated in the original finding, is at the seam: frames already transferred to a node but not yet pulled when rigd dies are baselined as "old" by the next run's PullWorker (run.py:145-147) and are therefore never pulled, renamed, or given a flight_log row — silently, though the images themselves remain on the camera card (store_dest:3) and in the node's PC-save dir and can be re-pulled via /api/shots. The operator is not left without a signal: the UI pill flips to "no run" live, run.json records final:false, and ~/rig/rigd.jsonl shows a "run started" with no matching "run stopped" and a "rigd up" in between. The missing capability is surfacing/repairing that state on restart, not recording it.
fix: Call runmgr.stop() from Rig.stop(), install a SIGTERM handler that routes to the same path, and on startup scan RUNS_DIR for run.json with final:false — rebuild frames/stats from the flight_log.csv files present, mark it final with an `interrupted: true` alert, and surface it once in the event log.

title: /api/shots re-lists and stat()s the entire never-pruned save directory on every 0.4 s poll, degrading the pull path as the deployment ages
goal_clause: "each image being taken <10ms from eachother" — measured degradation to 1.5 ms mean / 10 ms worst with dropped frames during sustained 2 fps runs
failure: /api/shots is O(N) in the size of the PC-save directory and nothing in the code ever prunes that directory, so the cost of the pull loop's 0.4 s poll grows with every frame the node has ever saved. Measured per-entry cost is 4.6 us on cam1 (Pi5) and 33 us on cam2 (Pi4), plus ~38 bytes of JSON per entry. The Pi4 node is the binding constraint: at roughly 10k accumulated frames /api/shots takes ~0.35 s, comparable to the poll interval itself, and at ~30k it takes ~1 s, at which point PullWorker's cycle (0.4 s wait + listing + downloads) can no longer keep up with a sustained 2 fps arrival rate. The consequence is a growing pull backlog and increasingly stale flight_log rows, and -- if the operator stops the run while the backlog is non-empty -- frames that were exposed but never pulled and therefore never entered the flight log (they remain on the node and the card, so they are recoverable manually). This has no effect whatsoever on inter-camera sync: firing is a locally scheduled absolute-epoch busy-wait inside piagent on port 8081, a separate process from ilxctl on 8080, so the measured 0.65 ms -> 1.5 ms skew degradation at 2 fps has a different cause. Reaching the problematic directory size requires roughly 1.5+ hours of continuous 2 fps capture on one camera with no operator clearing the save dir; rigd's disk_low anomaly (rigd.py:83-88, remedy "clear old frames from the PC-save dir") only fires around 200k frames, far past the point where the listing cost bites, so there is no alert on the axis that actually degrades first.
fix: Add an incremental listing (`/api/shots?since=<name|mtime>`) or a node-side archive/prune step at run start that moves already-pulled frames out of g_saveDir, and widen safeShotName to .arw so a RAW frame is at least visible and countable rather than silently absent.
